description: Q&A pairs grounded in 'Towards Federated Learning at Scale: System Design' (Bonawitz et al.). relevant_pages are the actual pages where each answer appears. Replace with your own corpus to evaluate other documents.

items.question: What is Federated Learning?
items.reference_answer: Federated Learning is a distributed machine learning approach that enables model training on a large corpus of decentralized data, keeping the data on users' devices instead of collecting it centrally.

items.question: What are the three phases of each round in the federated learning protocol?
items.reference_answer: Each round has three phases: Selection, Configuration, and Reporting. Devices check in and are selected, the server configures and sends the model and plan, and devices train locally and report updates back.

items.question: Which algorithm does the server use to aggregate the model updates from devices?
items.reference_answer: The server aggregates the reported device updates using Federated Averaging.

items.question: Under what conditions does on-device training run to avoid harming the user experience?
items.reference_answer: On-device training runs only when the phone is idle, charging, and connected to an unmetered network such as WiFi, to avoid impacting user experience, data usage, and battery life.

items.question: What are the main actor types in the FL server architecture?
items.reference_answer: The server architecture uses Coordinators, Master Aggregators, Aggregators, and Selectors. Coordinators orchestrate tasks, Master Aggregators manage rounds, and Selectors accept and forward device connections.

items.question: What is Secure Aggregation and what protection does it provide?
items.reference_answer: Secure Aggregation is a Secure Multi-Party Computation protocol that uses encryption so individual device updates are uninspectable by the server, which only sees the aggregated sum. It is deployed as a privacy enhancement.

items.question: What machine learning framework is the federated learning system built on?
items.reference_answer: The system is built on TensorFlow.
